@pablo-richard, my thinking was about having model data on the same grid as observation data:

Most (all?) global earth system models I know assume the planet to be a sphere, and run their simulations on the sphere. Lately, quite a few such models started to write their output to the healpix grid. For this mapping, they naturally use the latitude / longitude values of the sphere and apply the healpix pixelization without thinking about geographic / authalic etc...

Now, of course people like to compare model results to actual observations of the planet. To do so, those people who are using both, the model output and the observational data need to:
* find out which latitude on the (model-) sphere corresponds to which latitude of the (real-world) ellipsoid
* bring both datasets on the same grid

To find out which model-latitude corrsponds to which real-world-latitude, I think the best option is to use exactly what people did during the initialization phase of the model. In many cases (at least IFS and ICON) this initialization will be based on ERA5, which uses geographic latitude. We've also confirmed that people running NICAM model do the same. 👉 for most (all?) ESM outputs, we want to interpret their (spherical) latitude as geographic latitude when comparing with real world data. Thus, it seems useful to only have geographic latitudes when storing them as numbers (as @keewis wrote), to avoid mixing things up.

This brings us to the second problem: having both datasets on the same grid. While ERA5 itself (so far...) doesn't live on healpix, it still (kind-of) defines the healpix grid which is used by ESM-models, and that's the grid defined by geographic latitude. If now all the observational datasets end up on *another* healpix grid, defined by authalic latitudes (even though expressed as geographic latitudes), the cells of the healpix grid will be at different positions, thus requiring remapping between models and observations. I think this is a hard-to-solve conflict, and I don't know what best to do. I think there are three bad options:

* model on **geographic** healpix, observatios on **authalic** healpix (both are equal-area on their natural grid, so this seems to be the best choice for each domain, but cross-domain operations will be painful)
* model on **authalic** healpix, observations on **authalic** healpix (this seems to be the proper thing to do when talking about the real earth, but as models don't know about ellipsoids, doing this authalic-conversion will be super weird and will likely be done wrong in many cases. also the grid won't be equal-area anymore for the models...)
* model on **geographic** healpix, observatios on **geographic** healpix (this is the reverse of the second, however: observation people know about ellipsoids and probably won't screw it up, however, the healpix grid wouldn't be equal area for observatiosn)

Maybe this place is not the right one to discuss this, but we should do at some point and probably with a large community. My guess would be, that we'll end up with the first option if we don't coordinate early on, but it will be a pain in the long run. The two other options are both less perfect in their properties, but if we can agree on something in a large community, we might have much more fun in the long run when working with the data, because we don't have to regrid the data all the time.

PS: I'm not that sure anymore, how to think of equal area in terms of the models... maybe we should actually think of the ellipsoid before doing model-averages...

I think that the pixelation of the sphere resulting from healpix should be mapped in a unique way to the ellipsoid, with the choice of the (inverse) authalic mapping. Because:
1) this ensures equal area on the resulting pixelation of the ellipse while other mappings don't. 
2) having a unique ellipse pixelation would improve clarity by avoiding confusions with alternative pixelations. 
3) so far, I don't see the interest of using other alternatives*. The only limit I see for having a unique pixelation of the ellipsoid would be when dealing with a dataset defined on a very close but different pixelation, eg loading data defined on a grid obtained by (inverse) parametric (or reduced) mapping of healpix on the ellipsoid. In such cases, mapping the data from one grid to another would call for interpolations while the cells with reasonable depthes berely don't move relatively to their size. But anyway, the precision losses generated by these interpolations would remain smaller than the finest cells / resolution of the data.

If we choose to do so, I think we should drop the idea of having the `healpix_latitude_definition` parameter (since it would always be `authalic`). The `healpix_to_lonlat` function would end up in something like this:

```
def healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid, output_latitude_definition):
    lon, lat = _healpix_to_lonlat(...)  # the original function, operating on a sphere
    return lon, convert_latitude(lat, ellipsoid=ellipsoid,
                                 from_definition='authalic',
                                 to_definition=output_latitude_definition)
```

*@d70-t you mentioned the interest of getting closer to some observations such as ERA5. But since the latter does not rely on healpix, this data will have to be remapped anyway to be used with this package (and by the way, if I understood well the doc, it seems that ERA5 relies on a sphere model, WGS84 being used only for alignment purpose).

I agree with the view that the conversion is simply `healpix <-> sphere <-> ellipsoid`, but I don't think it is useful to return anything but the geographic (geodetic) latitude ($\phi$ in the schema): the authalic latitude ($\xi$) is a spherical latitude that is equal to the standard spherical latitude, and we only pass from spherical to ellipsoidal coordinates by converting to geographic.

This means that _all_ of the variants above (the single spherical latitude, WGS84 + geographic, and WGS84 + authalic) retain the equal area property if we use the appropriate formula to compute the cell areas (the cells for WGS84 + geographic are on the reference ellipsoid, while all others are on a sphere of varying radii).

It also means that passing ellipsoidal geographic coordinates to spherical healpix will result in something that's wrong (I'm still in the process of evaluating how much).

CF conventions already [have a way of defining the ellipsoid](https://cfconventions.org/Data/cf-conventions/cf-conventions-1.12/cf-conventions.html#appendix-grid-mappings), which likely should be reused for defining what `ellipsoid` would be in this particular case. I'd consider the latitude definition somewhat similar (but surely a different topic) to those ellipsoid-defining properties, and thus would expect the latitude definition to be at a similar place in CF conventions. Because of that, I wanted to suggest in [this comment](https://github.com/cf-convention/cf-conventions/issues/433#issuecomment-2891348122) that we might want to introduce such a convention in a separate CF issue.

I was wondering, if this really is a question of having healpix on different ellipsoids, or if this is somewhat independent of healpix, and more a question of which latitude to use? Here's my perspective on this:

healpix provides a mapping from cell-id <-> (any) latitude + longitude on a sphere. On a sphere, latitudes are uniquely defined, so there's no need to distinguish between different kinds of latitudes

Then, there's a mapping of latidudes between spheres and ellipsoids. This is not uniquely defined and described by [Karney 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.05818), and the choice is independent of using healpix or not. But to do healpix on an ellipsoid, we'd go healpix <-> sphere <-> ellipsoid.

Now, if we want to preserve the healpix equal area property on the ellipsoid, we likely want to choose authalic latitude for the sphere <-> ellipsoid mapping. But this would not change anything at all for the healpix <-> sphere computation, it's merely a choice of how we interpret the resulting latitude as a position on the ellipsoid.

The conversion would come into play, if we want to display the (authalic) latitudes as geodetic latitudes. This is something which likely would be needed, but it seems rather unrelated to healpix as such. It might still be useful to incorporate such a conversion into healpix-related functions, as this might lead to a simpler user interface, but in that case, I would expect to see two (or three, see later) user-parameters:
* the chosen ellipsoid
* the kind of latitude used for healpix <-> cell id mapping

I'd e.g. expect these three function calls to behave the same way (i.e., the same inputs and outputs, if we assume the returned latitude is always geodetic):

* `healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid="WGS84", healpix_latitude_definition="geodetic")`
* `healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid="sphere", healpix_latitude_definition="geodetic")`
* `healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid="sphere", healpix_latitude_definition="authalic")`

but I'd expect this one to behave differently:

* `healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid="WGS84", healpix_latitude_definition="authalic")`

All *but* the first ("WGS84", "geodetic") will have an equal-area property. However the first one would be the mapping most suitable to compare model data with observation data (e.g. [this is what ERA5 uses](https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/CKB/ERA5%3A+data+documentation#ERA5:datadocumentation-SpatialreferencesystemsandEarthmodel)).

---

One could go even futher and add a third argument (`output_latitide_definition`), which so far would always have been "geodetic". If this argument would exist, and we'd assume to have a function `convert_latitude(lat, ellipsoid, from_definition, to_definition)`, then we could implement `healpix_to_lonlat` as:

```
def healpix_to_lonlat(..., ellipsoid, healpix_latitude_definition, output_latitide_definition):
    lon, lat = _healpix_to_lonlat(...)  # the original function, operating on a shpere
    return lon, convert_latitude(lat, ellipsoid=ellipsoid,
                                 from_definition=healpix_latitude_definition,
                                 to_definition=output_latitide_definition)
```

As `convert_latitude(..., ellipsoid="sphere")` and `convert_latitude(..., from_definition=x, to_definition=x)`  (note: the same `x`) would be identity-functions in `lat`, this would also explain why the three above mentioned calls to `healpix_to_lonlat` should behave the same.
